I found the issue we need to address in our website's exporter: it generates resolution candidates, but it doesn't check whether VMMaker actually preserved those resolutions.

Your latest output gives us a useful starting point. In particular, 426×240, 427×240, and 428×240 were requested but not generated exactly, while 854×480 was generated as 856×480.

I'll update the exporter to distinguish exact matches from missing or altered resolutions, show the affected game names, and keep the original requested resolutions visible rather than silently substituting alternatives.

I've created the first version of our VMMaker Mode Audit tool.

Download VMMaker Mode Audit

It will:

  • Read VMMaker's generated modelines.

  • Compare them against the unique resolutions in our game database.

  • Identify exact matches, missing resolutions, and nearest generated alternatives.

  • Show the game names associated with each resolution.

  • Export the results to CSV.

For example, it will flag Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2's reported 426×240 mode rather than treating 424×240 as equivalent.

How to use it

  1. Upload vmmaker-audit.html to the root of your GitHub repository, alongside exporter.html.

  2. Open https://soho110.github.io/crt-game-database/vmmaker-audit.html.

  3. Paste your latest VMMaker generation output.

  4. Click Analyze modelines.

I attempted to update your GitHub repository directly, but GitHub returned a 403 permissions error. You'll need to upload this file manually.

One important distinction: This tool identifies the resolution mismatches; it doesn't yet make VMMaker generate unsupported widths. Our next technical task is determining whether those widths can be generated exactly with your AMD driver, or whether we must classify them as limitations for true 1:1 output.

Your existing VMMaker configuration and working Mina mode remain unchanged.

The audit tool is opening correctly, but it cannot find our game database. That's why the results table is empty and the Download results CSV button is disabled.

How to fix it

If you opened the HTML file directly from your Downloads folder, that's the likely cause. The tool expects this directory structure on GitHub Pages:

Plain text
crt-game-database/ ├── index.html ├── exporter.html ├── vmmaker-audit.html └── data/ └── games.json

  1. Open your GitHub repository: CRT Game Database.

  2. Verify vmmaker-audit.html is in the repository root, not inside another folder.

  3. Verify games.json is inside the data folder.

  4. Open the hosted version at VMMaker Mode Audit.

  5. Paste your 39 generated modelines and click Analyze modelines.

The tool uses the relative path data/games.json, so it should work when hosted alongside the database.

You don't need to change any VMMaker settings or regenerate your modelines. This is a website file-loading issue, not a CRT configuration problem.

Once the audit runs, we can identify which exact resolutions are missing and concentrate on fixing those rather than testing every game individually.
